entry.title: Catastrophic Overfitting is Weight Drift the Training Loss Cannot See
entry.summary:
Fast adversarial training (FAT) makes robust training affordable by replacing the multi-step attack with a single-step one, but it suffers from catastrophic overfitting (CO): partway through training, robustness to multi-step attacks collapses to near zero while the single-step attack used for training keeps being repelled. We show that CO is a quiet escape of the weights. Across the event the network's clean behavior quietly improves, and moving from the weights just before CO to those just after it changes the training objective only marginally while destroying most of the robustness.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory

entry.title: Rotom: A Microcontroller-Oriented Tweakable Block Cipher Using Modular Multiplication (Full Version)
entry.summary:
We propose Rotom, a family of 128-bit tweakable block ciphers designed for efficient software implementation on 32-bit microcontrollers. The central design idea is to use modular multiplication as a compact and software-efficient source of strong nonlinearity. Rotom instantiates this idea with a fixed 16-bit S-box built from odd constant multiplication modulo $2^{16}$ interleaved with lightweight linear maps, and combines it with a software-friendly recursive linear layer over four 32-bit words, a compact tweakey schedule, and modular-addition boundary key mixing.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Practical Optimal Bucket Sets with Power-of-Two Radices for LFG-Based MSM Algorithms
entry.summary:
Fixed point multi-scalar multiplication (MSM) is a major computational component of pairing-based SNARK proof generation. The Luo--Fu--Gong (LFG) framework is a variant of Pippenger's bucket method that uses a multiplier set $M$ and precomputed point multiples to reduce the number of buckets and online point additions. For radix $q$ and a positive multiplier set $M$, covering all digit residues requires a bucket set of size at least $q/(2|M|)$.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: LAMP: Linear Verification of Matrix Multiplication via Proximity Testing
entry.summary:
Verifiable computation systems often need to prove large matrix multiplication statements, but a direct SNARK arithmetization of a $k \times k$ product requires $\mathcal{O}(k^3)$ constraints. Freivalds' randomized check reduces the algebraic computation to vector-matrix products, but proving those products inside a SNARK still costs $\mathcal{O}(k^2)$ constraints. We present LAMP, a matrix-multiplication checking protocol that combines Freivalds' randomized check with proximity testing over linear error-correcting codes.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Bounded Information: PAC Certification of Multivariate Side-Channel Traces. Side-channel leakage certification aims to quantify what an attacker can learn about a secret variable from observed leakage.
entry.summary:
Side-channel leakage certification aims to quantify what an attacker can learn about a secret variable from observed leakage. Existing information-theoretic estimators, such as perceived information (PI), hypothetical information (HI), and nonparametric mutual information (MI), aim to quantify distributional leakage, but they become unstable in high-dimensional traces and do not provide a finite-sample certificate of the best attacker. We introduce \emph{Bounded Information} (BI), a probably approximately correct (PAC)-style finite-sample certification method that upper-bounds the exact-recovery success of a fixed attacker scope on unseen traces.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
